pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #17
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. Any white crystal used in cooking
   B. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. A mixture of two liquids

2. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 0 °C
   B. 37 °C
   C. 50 °C
   D. 100 °C

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   B. A chemical reaction forming ash
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. Movement of water only across a membrane

4. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Iron rusting
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Milk souring

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Water hardness? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Water hardness.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Water hardness.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Water hardness.

6. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Burning crop residue every week

7. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   C. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   D. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya

8. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Nutrition in animals? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Nutrition in animals.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Nutrition in animals.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Nutrition in animals.

9. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Interdependence of Life? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Interdependence of Life.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on The Interdependence of Life.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Interdependence of Life.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Metals and Alloys? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Metals and Alloys.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Metals and Alloys.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Metals and Alloys.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.

12. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Nitrogen gas only

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Structure of the atom and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Metals and Alloys and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Water hardness and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Nutrition in animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

2. D — 100 °C

3. A — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

4. C — Ice melting to water

5. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Water hardness.

6. C — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

7. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

8. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Nutrition in animals.

9. D — newton (N)

10. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Interdependence of Life.

11. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Metals and Alloys.

12. B — Glucose and oxygen

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Structure of the atom; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
